caption:
OCVSB Year 4:

There is no way to describe how beyond proud I am of this team. Anybody who knows me knows that I wanted to win state this season almost more than anything else; and although we didn’t finish our season with a W, I still believe that we won in heart ♥️ 
I keep getting asked, “How is it now that your season is over?” And I always respond, “It’s sad. But I’m not sad that we lost, just sad that it’s over.” And it’s true; I could not be any happier with the way this team has fought, grown, and persevered together. We competed as a TEAM and knew that no role was too small or too big for anybody. People doubted us, but we believed in each other and what we had. 
I would choose these girls over anybody, and the reality that this group doesn’t get to play together again still catches me off guard. We played every game for something bigger than ourselves, and it showed in our energy and grit. From beginning the pre-season unranked to achieving a program-best 3rd place finish at the Dave Kops TOC, and ultimately reaching the 6A semi-finals, this team demonstrated unwavering resilience through all the highs and lows.
I am so blessed for the 4 incredible years I spent with this program. I want to thank the coaches for devoting all of their time and wisdom to us, all the prior OCVSB players for showing me what kind of leader I wanted to be and the legacy I wanted to leave, all of our OCVSB parents for being our biggest supporters and for showing up to every game, and most importantly all of the girls for making this the best season ever 💙🦅

#TogetherEverybodyAchievesMore
#GTA #BBABB #OCVSB4Life

caption:
Words can’t even describe how this feels. You were taken from us too soon and it was all so sudden, but some things are just out of our control and that is what is so hard to grasp…why my Dad, why now. 

Thank you for everything you have done for me and all of the sacrifices you have made for this family. You are my hero and the best father a son could have asked for. I wouldn’t be the man I am today without you, because you instilled in me the principles of manhood. The boys and I did everything we could for you and I know you are proud of your son’s and will continue to look down proud as ever at what we accomplish in what we do in life. I can ease my mind knowing you are in a better place now and one day I’ll see you again. We will take care of mom for you and be her strongest soldiers. We miss you dad, and can’t wait to play catch with you like old times up above. 

Rest easy Dad, I love you dearly ❤️❤️❤️

@itz_zay_bytheway BIG ZAY‼️Not The Little One Xavier Williams is a standout young quarterback for the Park Hill Pirates. 🏴‍☠️At just 13 years old, he already shows impressive physical size for his age, giving him a strong presence in the pocket. What separates Xavier from his peers is his field awareness—he shows advanced 
📌understanding of coverages
📌anticipates pressure, and demonstrates the ability to go through progressions with composure. His footwork is clean for a player at this stage, and he displays natural leadership both in the huddle and on the sidelines.
Mechanically sound with a quick release and growing arm strength, Xavier is a high-upside prospect to monitor closely as he develops through the next levels of competition. With proper coaching and continued physical growth, he has the potential to become a top quarterback in his class in Colorado.

caption:
tb to the coolest trip I’ve ever been on. 

I had the most incredible opportunity to go to the Dominican Republic with some of my closest friends and tell people about Jesus back in June. one of the biggest take aways for me was that you don’t need to speak the same language to share the same love for the Lord. we were able to laugh, sing, dance, play sports, and so much more with the people there. 

our goal of the trip was to provide a way for these people to access free, clean water. we gave them filters from @filterofhope to filter the dirty water to clean water within a couple seconds. the main message was to share that before Jesus, our lives are dirty and impure just like the unclean water. With Jesus, our lives are clean and pure with his love. We gave them the gift of clean water along with new life. 

I have never met kinder or more welcoming people than the ones I got to spend time talking and laughing with there. if you have the opportunity to go on a missions trip, do it.

caption:
~~To think I almost said no to this trip 🤯
When I was invited to attend the Athlete Activism Summit and represent Rutgers, I was hesitant. I didn’t know if I was the right person for this opportunity. I wasn’t sure I had anything valuable to contribute, or if I truly belonged in a space like this. I am so glad that I decided to go.
Heading into the weekend, I was nervous. A new city, unfamiliar faces, and stepping way outside my comfort zone was intimidating. But the moment I walked into the hotel, I was welcomed with warmth, kindness, and a sense of belonging that I hadn’t expected. I realized I was exactly where I was supposed to be.
I came to the summit thinking I’d learn about allyship and how different schools support LGBTQ+ student-athletes. And I did. But I walked away with so much more. Real connections, powerful stories, and a community that helped me see myself differently.
Self acceptance has always been hard for me. Only recently have I started to embrace who I am. Hearing the experiences of others gave me more than just perspective, it gave me a choice. A choice to show up as my authentic self, even when I’m still figuring things out. It reminded me that we all deserve to live freely and fully.
One thing that stood out to me was a message repeated throughout the summit. “sports save lives”. I’ve always turned to softball in difficult times without fully realizing it. When I tore my ACL, it felt like a part of me was taken away. It showed me how deeply tied my identity is to the sport. I was fortunate to return, with the help of my physical therapist and athletic trainer. But not everyone is that lucky.
Some people lose their sport not because of injury, but because they choose to live truthfully and unapologetically. That should never be the cost of authenticity. No one should have to choose between who they are and the sport they love.
EVERYONE belongs in sports‼️
To everyone I met this weekend, thank you. Thank you for your stories, your openness, and for creating a space where people can be fully seen. You’ve helped me take another step toward becoming the person I want to be. You’ll always have a special place in my heart🫶🏼

caption:
man… where do I even start?

This past year at Stephen F. Austin have been nothing short of unforgettable. From a kid just hoopin’ to a champion — SFA didn’t just help me grow as a basketball player, it helped me grow as a person. The lessons, the love, the memories… unmatched.

To the entire coaching staff — y’all really stuck with me through the good and the bad. Forever grateful for y’all believing in me and pushing me to be my best.

To the trainers — appreciate y’all for keeping me iced up, and somehow ready to go every day (even when my body said otherwise). To the boosters, the fans, and everyone behind the scenes — THANK YOU. Y’all made Nac feel like home.

And to my teammates… man, we really went from 6am workouts….. to CHAMPIONS. Forever proud of what we accomplished together. That banner hangs forever.

This chapter might be closing, but this place? These people? These memories? Forever in my heart.

So long SFA… but never forgotten.

#OnceALumberjackAlwaysALumberjack #ThankYouSFA

caption:
when i was home a few weeks ago i made the decision to be baptized! this decision had been on my heart for a few months and i felt God had finally called me to take that next step in my faith. being renewed and made whole in Christ truly showed me His love is steadfast and unconditional. my past has made me into who i am today, but it does not define me. 

while externally i had everything i ever wanted, internally i felt broken, unfulfilled, and like i had truly lost myself. i pushed God away for so long, determined to figure things out on my own and it seemed my life was going in every direction except the right one. although my days were filled with “busyness” and people, i had never felt more lonely in my life. it wasn’t until i hit a peak of emptiness and isolation late in the fall semester that i turned to a random page in my Bible and started to just read. it was in that moment i felt a sense of peace and hope come over me that i hadn’t felt in years. i was finally getting what i had been looking for for so long, finally feeling a sense of security and worth that materialistic and worldly things couldn’t give me. from that day forward, i committed to growing in my faith and relying on God in every aspect of my life, fully believing His plan will always be greater than mine. when i look back to just 10 months ago, i’m in awe of how God has completely transformed me from the inside out. from writing in my notebook on September 29, 2024 “i just want to be done with gymnastics. i want to find a passion to live again. im at a loss, i just can’t do it anymore” to today, where i’m currently in the best mental state of my life and i feel my passion for gymnastics has gained a new and greater purpose, there’s no denying God did all of that. navigating a sense of self and worth knowing i am a daughter of the most high king has been such a refreshing and fulfilling journey that i know is far from over, and its so rewarding to see the story that continues to unfold. 

James 1:2-3 “Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds, because you know the testing of your faith produces perseverance.”

caption:
As I’ve grown up, I’ve realized that the other half of my heart has always been the person who created it in the first place. My Mom is the most selfless, kind, God-fearing woman I know. The last 6 years have been a true testament to my Mother’s character, as she has been in a fierce battle with congestive heart failure. Throughout her entire journey thus far, she has not been shaken. She continues to put others before herself, be a mentor and motherly figure to many, and make everyone feel at home in her presence. That’s just who she is. While she has stayed strong for those around her over these last 6 years, the time has come that her heart is finally giving up. My Mom is currently in the ICU in need of a heart transplant to save her life. As a psychologist, she has dedicated her life to helping others, but while she waits for a new heart, and will eventually need time to recover post-transplant, she is unable to work. Unfortunately, this adds immense financial stress to an already difficult time. So, if you are able, please consider joining me in supporting my incredible Mother. Any donations, reposts, or help you can offer means the world to us.

Mom, I will forever be indebted to you for everything you do for me. Thank you for showing up to my volleyball games despite your sickness. Thank you for inspiring me to cherish life in all its crazy ways. Thank you for supporting me even when you needed support the most. Thank you for loving me so gently and wonderfully. And most of all, thank you for being my guardian angel. If I could give you my heart, I would. 

GoFundMe link in bio❤️‍🩹

caption:
We can’t let this continue to happen. Suicide rates among student-athletes have doubled over the past 20-years. We have to start talking about our mental health. We have to do our part to de-stigmatize that which leads us to suffer in silence. We have to encourage each other to be vulnerable, to talk about the challenges we’re facing. The hustle of student-athlete life often leaves us disconnected, both from one another and from the essence of compassion. That’s why talking openly is so important. Conversations can uplift spirits, alleviate loneliness, and remind us of the power of genuine human interaction.
 
I recently started a movement called “Start a Conversation” in which I put forward this simple action step that all of us can take to begin the healing process...and that is, it’s time to say hello to more people, more often. For everyone who feels isolated, alone, or different, there’s 5 more out there who invariably feel the same way. The way you wish someone would say hello to you, is the same as those who wish you’d say hello to them.  Hello is a conversation starter. If not today or tomorrow, at some point the simple gesture of saying hello will start a conversation that may end up saving a life. And that life may even be your own. 
 
Please join me in the movement by agreeing to initiate more conversations about mental health.
 
 - Malcolm Johnson, Jr., Bowling Green State University football player

caption:
The Rams are excited to announce our new Quarterbacks Coach, Michael O’Connor! 

Originally from Orleans Ontario, Michael’s football journey has taken him through the highest levels of the game. From IMG Academy and Penn State, to leading the UBC Thunderbirds to a Vanier Cup championship, his experience speaks for itself. He was drafted by the Toronto Argonauts in 2019 and most notably played for the BC Lions alongside Nathan Rourke.

Most recently, Michael has competed with both Canada’s National Tackle Team and National Flag Team, earning gold at the GNC Championship in Germany — the first world competition since the 2015 IFAF World Championship.

Having spent time at every level of football, we know Michael will be a tremendous asset to our Rams family, and we can’t wait to see him help develop the next herd of winners.

“I Look forward to the opportunity to work with the Rams’ QBs. I love this game and I am passionate about mentoring the next generation!” - @15michaeloconnor

Welcome, coach!! 🐏

caption:
We at Innumeris are thrilled to congratulate Innumeris student and client, Jack Scullion, on earning a full-ride scholarship to Rutgers University to play American football! 🏈 Jack will be joining the prestigious Rutgers football team, an NCAA Division I program in the Big Ten Conference. We’re incredibly proud of Jack and his remarkable achievement! 🙌

Jack, a dedicated Gaelic Football player and U20 goalkeeper for Derry, transitioned to American football with support from the renowned partner academy of ours @leaderkicking, Leader Kicking. Leader Kicking honed Jack’s athletic skills, while Innumeris provided the essential academic support. 📚

Reflecting on his journey, Jack shared:
“I am so lucky that I had Innumeris education right by my side every step of the way when receiving my scholarship at Rutgers. I couldn’t fault Daniel or any of the team. They have been top class! They’ve helped me achieve my dream of playing American football in the biggest conference in the country.”

Our USA program is at the heart of Innumeris, and we’re excited to see our student-athletes like Jack pursue their dreams in the USA. 🇺🇸 We wish Jack the best of luck in his next chapter! 🌟

Interested in joining our next cohort? Contact us at Innumeris2020@gmail.com with your name, current school, year group, team you play for, and parent contact details.

Click on our bio for more info! 🔗

caption:
The Final Go Around is a senior season project presented by Hoop Diaries, created to highlight the journeys of selected seniors as they navigate their final year of high school basketball. For the 2024-25 season, I’ve chosen four seniors to follow closely-tracking their stories, learning more about them both on and off the court, and diving deeper into the moments that define their last ride.

After tearing her ACL in 2023 which sidelined her junior season. Precious was on a mission to make her senior year at Franklin High School one to remember. Not only through triumph and faith. She learned so much about her artisty in the recover process. She’s more than a hooper. Music, painintg, drawing and writing make her so ecletic off the court. Precious favorite form of art is murals. A class ran by Ms. Mac at Franklin High School is an art teacher who allows her students to explore all their creative avenues.

She’s been apart of 7 murals in the school, with 5 of them being her own. One thing Precious likes to speciallize in her art is her people. A black artists through thick and thin. Each works of art revolves around the crafts of showcasing her people. Her ‘Warrior Life’ and ‘Nas’ mural resemble more than just the people in her school, but how everyone can relate to the concept of showcasing who we are.

Headed back to basketball, the senior year didn’t go as planned, but it was about being a big sister to her teammates. Every squad goes through adversity and its best to be honest in those moments for the betterment of the team. It’s bigger than basketball and Precious is a walking example of that.

Lastly, Precious will be taking her talents into the Big-Ten conference at Rutgers University. She aims to use her platform not only to be a great player, but aspire girls just like her to chase their dreams.

Thank you Precious for allowing us to capture your senior year and we wish you nothing but the best!

caption:
Teamwork Turns Grind Into Greatness

Because no athlete becomes elite alone. Here’s why teamwork matters:

1. Shared Energy: When the team moves, motivation multiplies. You feed off each other’s drive.

2. Accountability: Teammates keep you honest. Every rep, every session. No shortcuts.

3. Growth Through Challenge: Training with others pushes you beyond what you’d do solo. Iron sharpens iron.

4. Support System: Wins feel bigger and setbacks feel smaller when you’ve got a crew behind you.

5. Collective Purpose: When everyone’s chasing the same goal, effort turns into synergy, and that’s where greatness happens.

caption: saying goodbye to playing for this program is one of the hardest things i’ve ever had to do. for the past 8 years i have been incredibly blessed to be part of the corona angels family that has done so much for me. since i was 10 years old, i have grown up in this family—being an angel made me tougher, a better player and person, and most importantly taught me what it means to be a strong woman. thank you to coach mike and gabe for taking me into the organization and for the next four years helped me develop. for the four years after that i was blessed to be coached by coach dom, dena, and marty. the tyson family has been so good to me. every text message, phone call, talk, and practice is what helped me grow into the person i am today. and i know in every part of me that the this family is always in my corner and will never leave my side. the most special thank you goes to mama donna for everything that she does for this program. when they say that the corona angels are a sisterhood, it is 100% true. i am so grateful for every teammate that i’ve ever had, that have turned into my forever sisters and my best friends. i never thought the day would come that i would take this jersey off for the last time, but i am nothing but grateful for the 8 years i’ve gotten to proudly wear corona angels across my chest. ca all day💙❤️

caption:
Isaiah 41:10 
Fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God;
I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.

Where do I even start. A few months ago I took a leap of faith and signed up for @theultimatetrainingcamp not knowing what to expect or what I would gain from this experience. I quickly realized how this was something that was truly one of a kind. I was accepted and loved by a community of God; I faced mental and physical battles that I wouldn’t have been able to do alone but only overcame with God. I’m thankful for every team member who helped me realize I am much more than my sport. This is was an experience I will never forget and I love every single person who made this a special experience. ❤️
